title: Rapid enrichment of mitochondria from mammalian cell cultures using digitonin
author: Dixit, Vanhoozer, et al.

steps.title: Maintain all steps on ice
steps.instruction: Perform every subsequent step with samples kept on ice.

steps.title: Count and harvest cells
steps.instruction: Harvest 1 × 10⁶–1 × 10⁸ cells per sample by trypsinization and count them using an Invitrogen™ Countess™ Automated Cell Counter.

steps.title: Wash cells and pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the harvested cells with 1 × PBS, then pellet them at 215 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in hypotonic buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 µL of hypotonic buffer and incubate on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Lyse cells with digitonin
steps.instruction: Add digitonin to lyse the cells and vortex intermittently.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 0.2 % high‑purity digitonin to achieve a final concentration of 0.02 % digitonin.
Vortex vigorously for 5–10 seconds every minute for a total of 5 minutes while keeping the sample on ice.

steps.title: Add isotonic buffer and low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (500 µL) of 2× isotonic buffer, then centrifuge immediately at 700 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove unbroken cells and debris.

steps.title: High‑speed spin to collect mitochondria
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant carefully to a new tube and centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C; discard the resulting supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction).

steps.title: Wash mitochondrial pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the mitochondria‑containing pellet without resuspending.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of 1× isotonic buffer on top of the pellet.
Invert the tube position and centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Store mitochondrial pellet at -80 °C
steps.instruction: Aspirate all supernatant completely and store the mitochondrial pellet at –80 °C until further use.
